description: Reorganize the test suite by Bounded Context, factor shared helpers and test data factories, add test categorization via [Trait], and enforce conventions with archtest rules. Five phases, each independently committable; green-bar invariant at every commit boundary.

tasks.title: Add Speed and Sut trait attributes to every spec test
tasks.description: Walk all 87 spec files in packages/server/tests/Mohist.Server.Tests/Specs/ and add [Trait("Speed", ...)] and [Trait("Sut", ...)] attributes to every [Fact] and [Theory]. Speed values: Unit (no fixture, no I/O), Grain (WorkflowGrainFixture/BacklogFixture), Integration (MohistIntegrationFixture.Client), Service (MohistDbFixture — only after Phase 2). Sut values mirror production Bounded Contexts: Workflow, Issue, Project, Epic, Runner, AgentSession, Skills, System, Api, Architecture, Foundation. Cross-cutting specs get multiple Sut traits. Run the verification script to confirm the trait vocabulary is complete and consistent.
acceptanceCriteria: Every [Fact] and [Theory] in the 87 spec files carries exactly one [Trait("Speed", ...)] attribute and at least one [Trait("Sut", ...)] attribute.
Speed value matches the fixture usage: WorkflowGrainFixture/BacklogFixture users get Grain, MohistIntegrationFixture.Client users get Integration, all other fixture users get Unit.
Sut values are drawn from the documented vocabulary (Workflow, Issue, Project, Epic, Runner, AgentSession, Skills, System, Api, Architecture, Foundation) and cross-cutting specs get multiple traits.
No spec test method is left without traits after the mechanical sweep (audit by grepping for [Fact] and confirming every match has [Trait] within 5 lines above).
tasks.output: 87 spec files updated with per-test [Trait] attributes; Speed and Sut counts recorded in the commit message for verification.
tasks.notes: Done in commit 7735b22b51. 87 spec files now carry Speed + Sut [Trait] attributes.

tasks.title: Document Speed and Sut trait vocabulary in Support/Traits.cs
tasks.description: Create packages/server/tests/Mohist.Server.Tests/Support/Traits.cs with two public static classes (Speed, Sut) that expose const string fields for each allowed value. This is the single source of truth for the trait vocabulary; future contributors see the choices at the call site via IntelliSense. Also document the migration rule from fixture type to Speed value in an XML doc comment on the Speed class.
acceptanceCriteria: Support/Traits.cs exists and declares Speed.{Unit, Grain, Integration, Service} and Sut.{Workflow, Issue, Project, Epic, Runner, AgentSession, Skills, System, Api, Architecture, Foundation} as public const string fields.
A future contributor can write [Trait(Speed.Unit, Sut.Workflow)] instead of magic strings without losing IntelliSense.
T-001's spec files can be refactored to use the constants in a follow-up commit; the trait values are byte-for-byte identical to the string literals used in T-001.
tasks.output: Support/Traits.cs with documented trait vocabulary.
tasks.notes: Done in commit 7735b22b51. Support/Traits.cs declares Speed.{Unit,Grain,Integration,Service} and Sut vocabulary as public const string fields.

tasks.title: Verify trait filtering works at the test runner level
tasks.description: Run the documented verification commands (dotnet test --filter Speed=Unit, Speed=Grain, Speed=Integration, Sut=Workflow) and capture timing measurements in the commit message. The Unit subset must complete in under 30 seconds. The full suite must still pass.
acceptanceCriteria: dotnet test --filter Speed=Unit runs only tests with [Trait("Speed", "Unit")] and completes in under 30 seconds on a developer workstation.
dotnet test --filter Speed=Grain runs only the WorkflowGrainFixture users and completes in under 90 seconds.
dotnet test --filter Speed=Integration runs only the WebApplicationFactory users and completes in under 180 seconds.
dotnet test (no filter) runs all 680+ tests and all pass.
Test counts under each filter match the audit performed in T-001.
tasks.output: Verification log captured in the commit message; CI updated to use Speed filters in follow-up PRs (out of scope for this change).
tasks.notes: Verified: Speed=Unit 4s / Speed=Grain 7s / Speed=Integration 7s. Full suite 22s. Committed in 7735b22b51 message body.

tasks.title: Extract ConfigureMohistServices extension from MohistServiceRegistration
tasks.description: Refactor packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Infrastructure/Hosting/MohistServiceRegistration.cs so the body of AddMohistServerCore (after the AddDbContextFactory line) is moved into a public static extension method ConfigureMohistServices(IServiceCollection services, IConfiguration configuration). The AddMohistServerCore method becomes a thin wrapper that calls the extension. The extension is then also callable from test fixtures. This catches drift where production code adds a service that tests forget to register.
acceptanceCriteria: ConfigureMohistServices extension method is public and lives in MohistServiceRegistration.
AddMohistServerCore behavior is byte-for-byte identical before and after the refactor: same services registered, same lifetimes, same order.
All 680+ existing tests still pass after the refactor.
The extension is reusable from test fixtures without copying the service graph.
tasks.output: MohistServiceRegistration.cs with extracted ConfigureMohistServices extension; AddMohistServerCore delegates to it.
tasks.notes: Done in commit 7c8f44ce22. ConfigureMohistServices is a public static extension on IServiceCollection. AddMohistServerCore is a thin wrapper.

tasks.title: Add MohistDbFixture for service-level specs
tasks.description: Create packages/server/tests/Mohist.Server.Tests/Support/MohistDbFixture.cs as a sealed class implementing IAsyncLifetime. It mirrors MohistIntegrationFixture's service graph (via the ConfigureMohistServices extension from T-004) but skips the WebApplicationFactory<Program> wrapper. It exposes IServiceProvider Services, IGrainFactory Grains, string ConnectionString, RecordingEventStore EventStore, InMemoryEventBus EventBus — but no HttpClient. The fixture initializes an in-memory SQLite database, the in-process Orleans test cluster, and the same DI graph as production.
acceptanceCriteria: MohistDbFixture exists and is a sealed IAsyncLifetime class.
InitializeAsync sets up SQLite in-memory + Orleans InProcessTestCluster + the production service graph (via ConfigureMohistServices).
DisposeAsync cleans up the SQLite keeper and Orleans cluster.
The fixture does NOT start a WebApplicationFactory, so its startup cost is under 3 seconds.
tasks.output: Support/MohistDbFixture.cs with full service graph and no WebApplicationFactory.
tasks.notes: Done in commit 7c8f44ce22. Support/MohistDbFixture.cs is a sealed IAsyncLifetime that mirrors production service graph without WebApplicationFactory.
